ios.desc:
PrecisionRush is a timing game about one thing: stopping the clock at exactly the right moment. It’s easy to learn, but genuinely challenging to master.

I built it to feel smooth and respectful of your time: no ads, no energy systems, no grinding. Just you, the timer, and your reflexes.

What’s inside:
Arcade Mode: Stop as close to the target as you can. Build streaks and push for higher scores.
Multiverse Mode: Track multiple stopwatches at once for a tougher challenge.
Daily Challenge: A fresh target every day, the same for everyone.
Battle Mode: Go head-to-head against adaptive AI opponents.
Zen Mode: Practice without pressure. No stakes, just timing.

Your score is based entirely on accuracy: no luck, no pay-to-win mechanics, no shortcuts. Just timing and consistency.

Earn XP, unlock achievements, build login streaks, and watch yourself improve over time. Clean visuals, satisfying effects, responsive controls, subtle haptics, and accessibility options like reduced motion.

If you enjoy the game as much as I do, there’s an optional “Support the Developer” tip feature.

PrecisionRush is a small game with a simple idea, but it rewards focus, patience, and the feeling of nailing that perfect stop.

show_hn.title: Show HN: PrecisionRush: a tiny timing game inspired by the iPhone stopwatch

quotes.text:
PrecisionRush is a small free iOS timing game I built solo. Weirdly enough, the idea came from playing with the default iPhone stopwatch and thinking: what if this was an actual game?

I’m not much of a gamer myself (I’ve only played a handful of games), but something about this tiny mechanic got stuck in my head, so I decided to build the version I personally wanted to play.

The premise is simple: you get a target time, you start the timer, and your goal is to stop it as close to the target as possible. If you land within ~20ms it feels almost unreal. It’s a tiny concept, but it turned out to be surprisingly addictive.

I shipped it last week and I’m currently in the “first real users” phase. I’ve only got a handful of ratings so far, but I’ve been genuinely happy just seeing people try it. One unexpected thing: a few users even tapped “Support the developer”, which I honestly didn’t think would happen.

I do this on the side and I’m definitely not a top game designer or UX person - I just like building small things I enjoy and iterating on them. I haven’t done any marketing yet and I’m not trying to sell anything here. I’d just love honest feedback from people who enjoy minimal games or quick skill tests:

- Does it stay fun after a few minutes, or does it get repetitive?
- Is the UI/feedback loop satisfying and clear?
- Anything obvious you’d improve or add?

App Store link: https://apps.apple.com/ro/app/precisionrush/id6755596108

Thanks for reading.
